acceptance_criteria: For a batch of (surface, r, u), WGSL returns the smallest positive root within tolerance of the CPU f32-cast Surface::distance across all 15 kinds; unit test vs CPU per surface type.
description: Port every SurfaceKind ray-intersection (planes, sphere, x/y/z cylinders, x/y/z cones, general Quadric quadratic, x/y/z torus quartic) from geometry/surface.rs into a WGSL compute kernel (f32): new src/gpu/shaders/surface_distance.wgsl + Rust wrapper in src/gpu/. Encode a surface as (kind_tag, coeff array). Mirror the CPU smallest_positive_root / quartic solver. Geometric foundation for the CSG distance search.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented in fa4449c (branch claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9). Deliverables: src/gpu/surface_distance.rs (encode_surfaces + SURF_STRIDE=12 layout; surface_distance_cpu_f32 scalar mirror for all 15 kinds incl. the derivative-bracketing quartic torus solver; surface_distance_gpu wgpu dispatch off-Android) + shaders/surface_distance.wgsl (return-by-struct polynomial solver, one thread per query).

VERIFIED on this GPU-less host: (1) cpu_f32_mirror_matches_f64_reference — f32 mirror vs trusted f64 SurfaceKind::distance over ~48 rays x origin lattice for every one of the 15 kinds, within 3e-3*(1+d); (2) coincident far-chord case; (3) wgsl_shader_is_valid — naga parse+full validation of the WGSL (well-formed, type-checks, no GPU needed). 162 lib tests pass; Android lib check clean (CPU mirror Termux-safe; GPU path + naga dev-dep gated off Android).

STILL OWED before close (acceptance says 'WGSL returns ... within tolerance'): the GPU-vs-mirror gate gpu_matches_cpu_reference currently SKIPs here (no adapter) — it must be run GREEN on a real GPU host to confirm on-hardware execution matches the mirror. Also owed: human review (AI-draft per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md). Leaving CLAIMED, not closed, until the on-hardware gate passes.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
ON-HARDWARE GATE IS NOW SATISFIABLE AND RAN GREEN, 2026-08-11 (observed while working op-nhoa on a different host from the 2026-07-24 pass).

The 2026-07-24 comment left one thing owed: 'the GPU-vs-mirror gate gpu_matches_cpu_reference currently SKIPs here (no adapter) - it must be run GREEN on a real GPU host to confirm on-hardware execution matches the mirror.' THIS HOST HAS AN ADAPTER.

EVIDENCE (commands actually run):
  cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --release gpu::surface_distance::tests::diagnose -- --nocapture --ignored
    adapter : NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050
    backend : Vulkan

    kernel needs storage buffers: 7 -> supported? true

  That diagnostic obtains its context from crate::gpu::probe(), so probe() returns Some on this host, which means gpu_matches_cpu_reference (surface_distance.rs:1581-1585) takes the GPU branch rather than its no-adapter early return.

  cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --release gpu::surface_distance -- --nocapture
    8 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the diagnostic). gpu_matches_cpu_reference ... ok
    hybrid_splits_work_across_both_devices ... ok
  Also green in the same session: gpu::batched_flight::gpu_flight_matches_cpu_mirror, gpu::batched_event::gpu_event_matches_cpu_mirror, gpu::union_grid (both), gpu::xs_interp::gpu_matches_cpu_reference. Full lib suite 212 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored, release mode.

HONEST SCOPE OF THIS OBSERVATION: I did not re-derive the acceptance criteria or review the kernel; I ran the existing tests on a GPU host and they passed. The test asserts GPU vs the f32 CPU mirror at tol = 1e-3*(1+d) across all 15 SurfaceKind over ~48 rays x a 27-point origin lattice. The other item the 2026-07-24 comment left owed - human review of the AI-drafted kernel per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md - is UNCHANGED and still outstanding. Not closing.

title: outram-mc GPU: surface distance-to-surface kernel (WGSL, all 15 SurfaceKind)

description: Blender's Bisect. Cut a mesh by a plane (point + normal) and keep the half where n.(x-point) <= 0, clipping every face against the half-space with Sutherland-Hodgman. New crossing vertices deduped per undirected original edge so adjacent faces share them. Leaves the cut open (composes with fill_holes to cap). Directly serves the CSG/MC half-space workflow. New MeshOp::Bisect { point, normal }. V&V: cube[-1,1]^3 bisected by z=0 (+z) -> open half-box; fill_holes(that) -> watertight chi=2 with signed volume = 4 (half of 8); plane fully outside keeps mesh unchanged; plane fully inside-out yields empty mesh.
title: outram-blender: bisect (plane cut / half-space clip)

description: async-opcua server in its own thread with its own tokio runtime, bridging the shared CIET state. Writable nodes: heater power kW, CTAH pump pressure Pa, CTAH/TCHX outlet set points degC, frequency-response amplitude/frequency/steady-state power, branch blocking, timestep. Readable nodes: heater power, BT-11/12/21/27/41/43/60/65/66, FM-20/40/60, mixing nodes, sim time, calc time. PKI dir at ~/.outram-park/ciet_v2_pki (%APPDATA%\\outram-park on Windows). Default: SecurityPolicy::None + anonymous, loopback-only — educational toy, no security by design; must be documented as such.
title: ciet_v2: OPC-UA server on a parallel thread
